title: Strict-local projective-line exchange
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a local homomorphism of strictly henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], with induced residue-field extension $\bar\varphi:\kappa_A\to\kappa_B$. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$, $X=\mathbf P^1_S$, $X'=\mathbf P^1_T$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], and let $(g':X'\to X,p':X'\to T,p:X\to S,g)$ be the base-change square. Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$, and $q\geq0$. Write $i:X_0=\mathbf P^1_{\kappa_A}\to X$, $j:X'_0=\mathbf P^1_{\kappa_B}\to X'$ for the closed fibres, $k:X'_0\to X_0$ for the map induced by $\bar\varphi$, $F_0=i^{-1}F$, and $t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa_B\to T$ for the closed geometric point [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Under the canonical global-germ identifications followed by closed-fibre restriction [def-weil-pbc-derived-global-germ; def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], the degree-$q$ stalk at $t$ of the exchange [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is the map
$$k^*:H^q(X_0,F_0)\longrightarrow H^q(X'_0,k^{-1}F_0).$$
More precisely these canonical identifications $e_1:(g^{-1}R^qp_*F)_t\simeq H^q(X_0,F_0)$ and $e_2:(R^qp'_*g'^{-1}F)_t\simeq H^q(X'_0,k^{-1}F_0)$ satisfy $e_2\circ\mathrm{Ex}_t=k^*\circ e_1$. If $\bar\varphi$ is an isomorphism, $\mathrm{Ex}_t$ is an isomorphism.

proof.text: The residue quotient maps satisfy $\bar\varphi\circ r_A=r_B\circ\varphi$: both send $a$ to the residue class of $\varphi(a)$. Hence the induced projective-line square satisfies $g'\circ j=i\circ k$. Indeed projective lines are the products of their bases with the fixed projective line over $\mathbf Z$, and both composites have the same two projections. This also identifies $j^{-1}g'^{-1}F$ with $k^{-1}i^{-1}F$ via the inverse-image composition isomorphisms.

proof.text: Let $U=H^q(X,F)$ and $V=H^q(X',g'^{-1}F)$. Use the canonical derived global germs, precomposed with inverse Leray as defined, and take degree $q$. This gives maps $\alpha:U\to(g^{-1}R^qp_*F)_t$ and $\beta:V\to(R^qp'_*g'^{-1}F)_t$. They are isomorphisms: the two underived germ transformations are natural isomorphisms by the strict-local global-germ lemma; deriving them preserves their inverses, as does taking homology, and the Leray factors are isomorphisms. The exact-stalk identification is the one specified in the definition of the derived global germs. Apply the canonical derived global-germ exchange identity to $F[0]$. The derived-unit description of cohomology pullback identifies its middle arrow with $(g')^*$, giving $\mathrm{Ex}_t\alpha=\beta(g')^*$. No arbitrary choice of additive equivalences is made.

proof.text: The inverse-image stalk isomorphism identifies every stalk of $g'^{-1}F$ with a stalk of $F$. These groups are torsion, so the stalkwise characterization of torsion implies that $g'^{-1}F$ is torsion. Apply the strictly henselian projective-line comparison over $A$ to $F$ and over $B$ to $g'^{-1}F$. Thus the actual restrictions $r=i^*:U\to H^q(X_0,F_0)$ and $s=j^*:V\to H^q(X'_0,j^{-1}g'^{-1}F)$ are isomorphisms, in every degree including zero.

proof.text:
Let $c_{g',j,F}$ and $c_{i,k,F}$ be the unit-compatible composition isomorphisms of step 1, with their common target identified using $g'\circ j=i\circ k$. Put $\gamma=c_{i,k,F}^{-1}\circ c_{g',j,F}:j^{-1}g'^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}k^{-1}i^{-1}F$ and $\tilde s=H^q(\gamma)\circ s$. Clause 4 of cohomology-pullback functoriality gives $H^q(c_{g',j,F})s(g')^*=(g'\circ j)^*=(i\circ k)^*=H^q(c_{i,k,F})k^*r$. Composing with $H^q(c_{i,k,F}^{-1})$ gives $\tilde s(g')^*=k^*r$. Set $e_1=r\alpha^{-1}$ and $e_2=\tilde s\beta^{-1}$. For a stalk element $x$ the identity of step 2 gives $\beta^{-1}\mathrm{Ex}_t(x)=(g')^*\alpha^{-1}(x)$, and hence
$$e_2\mathrm{Ex}_t(x)=\tilde s(g')^*\alpha^{-1}(x)=k^*r\alpha^{-1}(x)=k^*e_1(x).$$
These are precisely the canonical global-germ and closed-fibre identifications specified in the statement.

proof.text: If $\bar\varphi$ is an isomorphism then $k$ is an isomorphism: its inverse is base change of $\operatorname{Spec}(\bar\varphi^{-1})$, and the two composites are identities by their projections to the base and fixed projective line. By the composition and identity laws for cohomology pullback, pullback along $k^{-1}$ is inverse to $k^*$ after the canonical coefficient identifications. Thus $k^*$ is invertible. The formula of step 4 yields $\mathrm{Ex}_t=e_2^{-1}k^*e_1$, an isomorphism.
